narr: Significant flash flooding occurred over west Kentucky, as anomalously high amounts of low-level moisture streamed northward over a warm front that became stationary along the Tennessee border. Steady rains began just after 0000CST on the 15th and continued until around 0100CST on the 16th. The rain came in waves with the first one targeting Fulton, Murray, Fort Campbell, and Guthrie with 1-2��� in the pre-dawn hours. The first flash flooding report came from Guthrie where flood waters had closed several roads and surrounded a few homes by 0430CST. By 1200CST the continuous rains had created a swath of 2-5��� of rainfall over the southern half of the Purchase Area and along and south of the Interstate 69 corridor. The heavy rain (1-2) resulted in a rock slide that closed the right lane of eastbound Interstate 69 about 3 miles west of Dawson Springs in Caldwell County in the late morning. Numerous roads were impassable due to flash flooding of creeks and rivers. The South Fork of the Little River swelled to its major flood level resulting in widespread road closures in Hopkinsville. Its crest of 20.16 at the Bypass site was the third highest crest every recorded at that location. After a brief lull in the mid to late afternoon, a line of thunderstorms pushed eastward across the hardest hit areas near the Tennessee border in the evening. Small hail, up to 0.7��� in diameter, was reported in Hazel, Murray, Newstead, Pembroke, and Trenton. Gusty winds up to 50 mph were reported from Earlington and Nortonville to Central City. As the heavy rain diminished in the late evening, major flooding developed along the Clarks River, flooding a firehouse and a pair of homes in Almo. The worst flooding occurred downstream in Benton, where several feet of water inundated businesses and closed numerous roads on the east and north sides of town. Two people lost their lives after their vehicles were swept away by flood waters, one in Caldwell County and the other in Graves County. There were numerous successful water rescues performed after vehicles stalled out in flood waters or were swept away. Final rainfall totals ranged from around 3��� near the Ohio River to nearly 7��� over much of the Jackson Purchase, including Fulton, Mayfield, Murray, and Benton, and northeast through Princeton and Central City. Daily rainfall records for the 15th were set at Paducah (4.54), Poplar Bluff (3.23), and Evansville (3.07).
ev: Flash flooding has closed Highway 1943 at Skin Frame Creek and Highway 819 at Panther Creek. Several county roads also flooded in the same areas.
Flash flooding along Goose Creek closed Highway 128 southeast of Princeton.
Flash flooding closed Alternate U.S. 41 near the Webster County line.
Flood waters isolated the Evergreen Apartments in Hopkinsville. Several nearby roads were water covered and impassable.
Much of Highway 121 from New Concord southeast to the state line was impassable due to flood waters.
Flash flooding inundated roads and threatened homes in the Guthrie area.

Flash flooding made several roads in Pembroke impassable, including Mason Lane at Highway 115, Spring Street, and south Main Street. Flood waters were just deep enough to get into two homes on East Nashville Street in Pembroke.

Torrential rainfall during the evening hours, following the heavy rain from the earlier round, resulted in flash flooding issues on the north and east side of Benton with multiple roads closed. Flooding issues transitioned to areal flooding overnight with the highest water levels in the town of Benton occurring the following day with the arrival of extremely high waters on the Clarks River.
One person was rescued from a vehicle stranded in high water on Clayton Drive east of Murray.
Flooding along the Clarks River and Bee Creek closed numerous roads in and around Murray.
Water covered a portion of Highway 94 between Murray and Lynn Grove.
Flash flooding along Brush Creek closed Highway 58 and Highway 1283 near the Hickman County line.
Flood water from Mayfield Creek closed Highway 408 east near Viola.
Flash flooding has covered the road on U.S. 51 near the intersection with Highway 1529.
Flash flooding along the Little Bayou de Chien east of Cayce closed Highway 94.
Flood water closed a portion of Highway 94 3 to 4 miles west of Hickman.
Flood waters made portions of New Hope Road and Hardy Road impassable.

Brushy Grove Creek flooded Highway 126 making it impassable. Portions of Wallonia Road (Highway 128) and Barefield Road (Highway 1507) were also closed due to flood waters. The flooding was generally centered around the community of Cerulean.

Flood water from the Clarks River was 2 to 4 inches deep in the Calloway County Fire-Rescue substation in Almo. The substation has never flooded before. Flood water caused minor damage to a nearby home and got into the crawl space of another.
Flood water from Cane Creek flooded a garage and surrounded a house on Tater Road northwest of Wingo.

Flood waters have closed Highway 307 from Highway 58 in Fulgham southward to the Fulton County line. Every State Highway across Hickman County now has water over it in at least one location, with the exception of Highway 239.
Flash flooding closed Highway 58 near the Graves County line.
Widespread flooding surrounded a mobile home on Highway 80.
Flash flooding along Mayfield Creek closed a portion of U.S. 62 east of Cunningham.
Flash flooding closed a portion of Highway 80 just west of Arlington.
Highway 1255/Bonds Road was closed due to flash flooding.
Flash flooding closed Highway 855 between Frances and New Salem.
Flash flooding washed out portions of several county roads.
Flash flooding closed a portion of U.S. 62 near Nortonville.
Flash flooding closed a portion of Highway 1379 northeast of Central city. Several other county roads were also closed from Central City to Powderly and Greenville.
Flash flooding closed a portion of Highway 138 near Slaughters.
A water rescue occurred along Slaughters Elmwood Road north of Slaughters due to flash flooding along the Sugar Camp Creek.
A water rescue occurred on Highway 132 between Dixon and Clay due to flash flooding along Crab Orchard Creek.

Nearly two dozen roads were closed due to flash flooding as of 4 PM. The flash flooding intensified in the early evening, as a line of thunderstorms moved through the region. Highway 298 was closed just west of Masonville, and Highways 762 and 764 were closed near the Ohio County line.
Flash flooding along Yellow Creek, closed a portion of Highway 797 southeast of Beech Grove. One water rescue occurred in this location. Numerous other county roads were flooded across McLean County.
A water rescue occurred on Highway 109 near Wheatcroft due to flash flooding along the Caney Fork.
Flash flooding closed a portions of Highway 902 near the Dry Branch.

A bridge on KY-58 lost much of its support due to flash flooding damage. The scale of damage was observed once waters receded during the afternoon the day after torrential rainfall. End time based on observation of damage.
A portion of Highway 1014/Houser Road was closed due to flash flooding.

7 roads underwater as of late afternoon, mainly near creeks.
